sentences.text: Shri Abhinav Dhanodkar, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Manoj Munshi, learned counsel for the respondents.
Heard finally with consent.
By this writ petition, the petitioner has challenged the impugned notices date 1/9/2017 Annex.P/1 by which the stock of polythene bags of the petitioner has been seized and the sample has been taken.

The case of the petitioner is that it is engaged in the business of manufacture and retail sale of plastic bags and that the respondents had visited the petitioner's premises on 8/7/2017 and had sealed it on the basis of mere doubt and suspicion.
Thereafter, on 1/9/2017 the notice of seizure was served upon the petitioner against which the petitioner had submitted representation dated 10/10/2017 but no action has been taken till now.
According to the petitioner, the entire impugned action of the respondents is contrary to applicable provisions of the Act & rules.
A reply has been filed by the respondents taking the stand that the petitioner is not a manufacturer but he is only a retailer in plastic products.

Further plea has been taken that the petitioner was engaged in trading of carry bags and plastic bags having thickness of less than 50 microns which is not permissible under Rule 4 (d) of the Waste Management Rules,
2016 and that the petitioner has violated the provisions of Madhya Pradesh Jaiv Anaashya Apashishta (Niyantran) Act,
 ~2~
2004.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Further plea has been raised that on receiving the intimation about storage of huge quantity of prohibited plastic products, the petitioner has taken action of seizing the prohibited goods in terms of the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act and that after the seizure the criminal prosecution of the petitioner will be started where he will have full opportunity to defend himself before the JMFC.
 Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that Shri Gautam Bhatiya, the Food Safety Officer had no authority to issue the seizure notice Annex.P/1 and seize the petitioner's goods.

Further plea has been raised that the petitioner's godown has been locked and the respondents are not opening the lock thereof inspite of the representation and that the requisite procedure for seizure has not been followed.

As against this, learned counsel for respondents submits M/S Ratnesh Packaging Thru.Surendra ... vs Indore Municipal Corporation on 14 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21949840/
1

sentences.text: that the concerned Food Safety Officer was the authorized officer in terms of the Act and that the due procedure was followed and since the petitioner was retailing the prohibited item, therefore, action has been taken against him and that the act of the petitioner was an offence within the provisions of the Act, therefore, at the stage of prosecution, the petitioner will have full opportunity to defend himself.
He further submits that if the petitioner wants to get the seized item released he is required to approach the JMFC by filing an application for Supurdagi.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of record it is noticed that the impugned notice and the seizure has been done under Section 10(1)(C) of the  ~3~
Environmental (Protection) Act, 1986 which provides as under:-
 "10. Powers of entry and inspection-(1) Subject to the  provisions of this section, any person empowered by the  Central Government in this behalf shall have a right to  enter, at all reasonable times with such assistance as he  considered necessary any place-  ...........
(c) for the purpose of examining and testing any equipment, industrial plant, record, register,
document or any other material object or for conducting a search of any building in which he has reason to believe that an offence under this Act or the rules made thereunder has been or is being or is about to be committed and for seizing any such equipment, industrial plant, record, register,
document or other material object if he has reasons to believe that it may furnish evidence of the commission of an offence punishable under this Act or the rules made thereunder or that such seizure is necessary to prevent or mitigate environmental pollution."
Under the aforesaid provision, the person empowered by the Central Government is entitled to seize the material.
The impugned notice has been issued by Gautam Bhatiya, Food Safety Officer.

The respondents have placed on record a copy of notification dated 4/8/2011 published in the Madhya Pradesh Gazette on 5/10/2011 by which Shri Gautam Bhatiya has been appointed as Food Safety Officer for the local area of his jurisdiction in terms of Section 37 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

Counsel for the respondents has produced a copy of the notification No. SO 83(E) dated 16/2/1987 issued under Section 10 and notification No. SO 84(E) dated 16/2/1987 under Section 11 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 whereby the Food Inspectors have been notified as the ~4~
empowered authority in terms of Sections 10 and 11 of the Act.
Hence, the contention of counsel for the petitioner that the seizure notice has been issued and the seizure has been done by the incompetent authority is found to be devoid of any merit.

So far as the issue of following the procedure prescribed in Rule 6 of the Environment (Protection)
Rules, 1986 is concerned, learned counsel for the respondents has rightly drawn the attention of this Court to the Panchnama Annex.R/1 filed along with the reply which reveals that the seizure has M/S Ratnesh Packaging Thru.Surendra ... vs Indore Municipal Corporation on 14 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21949840/
2 been done after following the due procedure.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner has failed to point out from these Panchnama that any of the requirement of the Rule has not been complied with or any illegality in this regard has been done.

That apart it is also noticed that vide notification dated 24/5/2017 issued under Section 3 of the Madhya Pradesh Jaiv Anaashya Apashishta (Niyantran) Act, 2004, the State Government has imposed a complete ban on the production, storage transportation, sale and use of plastic carry bags in the entire State of Madhya Pradesh.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Jaiv Anaashya Apashishta (Niyantran) Act, 2004
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Hence there is no substance in the submission of counsel for petitioner that impugned notice has been issued without the authority of law.

This Court in order to ascertain the correct position on the spot, vide order dated 12/1/2018 had appointed Commissioner for spot inspection and the report of the Commissioner reveals that only the godown of the petitioner has been sealed.
The record reflects that the petitioner has already approached the respondent No.1 by filing the application dated 3/7/2017 for opening the seal of the godown.
~5~ Learned counsel for the respondents has no objection in considering the said application within a time bound period.

Having regard to the aforesaid, the present writ petition is disposed of without interfering in the seizure notice Annex.P/1 but by directing respondent No.1 to take appropriate decision on the petitioner's application dated 31/7/2017 in accordance with law within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
C.C. as per rules.

(Prakash Shrivastava) Judge BDJ M/S Ratnesh Packaging Thru.Surendra ... vs Indore Municipal Corporation on 14 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21949840/
